questions.text: Why does an R_X86_64_PLT32 call relocation in an object not guarantee that the linked call uses a PLT entry?

options.A: The compiler has already resolved every external address before linking.
options.B: PLT32 records apply only to data pointers, never function calls.
options.C: The dynamic loader removes all call instructions before execution.
options.D: The linker can resolve a function defined in the inputs as a direct call.

questions.explanation: The linker decides from symbol resolution. Defined input functions can become direct calls; unresolved external functions may need PLT entries and GOT slots.

questions.text: A stripped arm64 Mach-O executable has almost no names in nm. Which approach best recovers and evaluates its function starts in this lesson?

options.A: Count the remaining names and report that as the function count.
options.B: Read LC_FUNCTION_STARTS and score its starts against an unstripped twin.
options.C: Scan only for one prologue pattern and assume every function uses it.
options.D: Treat every aligned instruction as a separate function start.

questions.explanation: The link editor’s function-start table survives stripping in the fixtures. Comparing against the unstripped twin gives measurable coverage; optimized leaf functions can lack the scanned prologue.

questions.text: The chained-fixup walker extracts nxt = (raw >> 51) & 0xfff, stops for nxt == 0, and otherwise advances offset += nxt * 4. With offset=0x4000 and nxt=2, where is the next fixup?
questions.explanation: The next field is measured in four-byte units. Two units advance eight bytes, from 0x4000 to 0x4008.
